full_judgment:
Habibur Rahman Khan, J.: This is an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed at the instance of the accused-petitioners, Haji Obaidul Haque and Mrs. Jahanara Begum, Directors of Janata Fibres International Limited, and a Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Narayanganj and also on the opposite party No. 2 Mr. M. Bazlul Bari, Deputy General Manager (Regional). Sonali Bank, Bangabandu Road. Narayanganj, to show cause as to why the proceedings in G.R. Case No. 126 of 1986 arising out of Narayanganj P.S. Case No.7(5)86 dated 5.5.86 under Sections 420/405/ 409/ 457/471/511 and 109 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 now pending before the Upazila Magistrate. Narayanganj should not be quashed so far as it relates to the petitioners pending hearing of the Rule the proceedings of G.R. Case No. 126 of 1986 was also stayed. 

 2. Facts of the case, Relevant for the disposal of the Rule are and as follows: 

 Mr. Bazlul Bari, Deputy General Manager, Regional office of Janata Bank, Bangabandhu Road, Narayanganj, as the complainant lodged the F.I.R. under Sections 420/405/ 407/ 409/ 468/114 of the Penal Code with Narayanganj Police Station, against the petitioners and 4 others being Narayanganj P.S. Case No.7(5)86, alleging inter alia, that the Managing Director of Janata Fibres International Limited (Now dead) in collusion with the Assistant General Manager, Mr. Ashrafuzzaman Bhuiya, Second officer, Mr. Shafiuddin Ahmed and Export Officer Mr. Naresh Chandra Bhowmik of Janata Bank, Bangabandhu Road Branch, Narayanganj, has committed breach of trust by misappropriating bank's money to the misappropriating extent of Taka 2,08,35,000/- (Taka two crore eight lacs thirty five thousand) only by obtaining loans from the Bank against packing credit through deceitful means submitting fake, forged and fraudulent 6 Barge Receipts allegedly issued by Amazon Shipping Line of 21, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka, and thus cheated the Bank. The said Inland Carrier, in fact, did not issue the said Barge Receipts and carried the jute goods of the petitioners Company Janata Fibres International Limited. The said Packing Credit was allowed by the bank to the petitioners' company on 5.5.1985. It was also alleged that the Managing Director of the said company committed breach of trust by misappropriating bank's money to the extent of Taka 1,19,11,000/- (Taka one crore nineteen lacs eleven thousand) by obtaining loans from the Bank against Packing Credit through deceitful means by submitting fake, forged and fraudulent Barge Receipts allegedly issued by Bangladesh River Service of 560, Nayatola, Maghbazar, Dhaka, and thus cheated the Bank. The said Inland Carrier in fact did not issue the said Barge Receipts and carry the jute goods of Janata Fibres International Limited. The said Packing Credit was allowed by the bank to the said Managing Director on various dates from 4.3.1986 to 3.4.1986. The Managing Director of the company authorised payment to the extent of Taka 19,20,054/58 paisa (nineteen lacs twenty thousand fifty four and paisa fifty eight) only through cheques with the help of Assistant General Manager of the said Bank during the period from 18.8.1985 to 2.8.1985 from the cash credit account of his company Janata Fibres International limited. 

 3. The petitioners Nos. 1 and 2 having learnt about the case voluntarily surrendered before the Magistrate and they Acre granted bail by the Magistrate on 15.2.1987 and since then they are continuing on bail and the said Managing Director (Hemayetuddin) was also granted bail by the learned Sessions Judge. Narayanganj, and thereafter died while on bail. 

 4. In the application under Section 5617 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the petitioners have sought for quashment of the criminal proceedings pending against them stating inter-alia that the petitioners are the directors of Janata Fibres International Limited. They are respectable rich and reputed businessmen and have been carrying on various types of business in jute and jute goods having establishment all over Bangladesh. The Managing Director of the company, Janata Fibres International Limited, had been maintaining various accounts of the company with Janata Bank, Nitaiganj Branch, and thereafter, also with the Bangabandhu Road Branch, Narayanganj, since 1976 and had been making business deal through Janata Bank as a regular customer. The petitioners are innocent of the charges brought against them and the allegations made in the F.I.R. and the charge sheet are absolutely false, frivolous aid malafide. Moreover, these allegations on the every face of it do not constitute any criminal offence as it would appear from the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 5. It is stated that the petitioners' company, Janata Fibres International Limited, entered into a contract with a foreign company named Charge Tex Co. Ltd., Tehran, Iran, being Contract No. JBIU Targeted/Agreement / 84-85 dated 20.10.84 for supply of 2000 M. Tons of BTC i.e. 11,100 bales of BTC. And the said foreign buyer agreed to buy the aforesaid jute goods at the rate of $880.00 and & 870.00 per M. Ton respectively depending upon its quality. Accordingly, the petitioners' company, Janata Fibres International Limited, obtained Packing Credit facility to the extent of Taka 3,08,35,000/- (Taka three crores eight lacs thirty five thousand) only on 5.5.1985 by submitting 6(six) barge receipts issued by the Inland Carrier Amazon Shipping Line in due course of banking business showing carriage of the aforesaid bales of jute; aforesaid 8200 bales of jute were dispatched to Mongla port under the above barge receipts, the foreign buyers declined to take delivery of the said goods due to sudden fall of price of jute in the International market. The said foreign buyer refused to place any vessel at the Chalna Port and also refused to send L/C in the case. And as a result, the entire consignment was shut up at the Mongla Port. The petitioners' company, however, succeeded in selling 4898 bales of jute to other foreign buyers and 1302 bales to the local buyers out of 8,200 bales and remaining 2000 bales were brought back from Chalna Port and were pledged with the bank and the bank adjusted the Packing Credit of the petitioners' company with the sale proceeds of Taka 1, 00,000/- (Taka one lac) only on the export of jute to the above named foreign buyers. As a result the margin of Packing Credit account was reduced by the bank from Taka 3,08,35,000/- to Taka 2,08,35,000/- and that amount (Taka. 2,08,35,000/-) has been shown in the F.I.R. as the amount alleged to be misappropriated by the petitioners without giving any explanation in the F.I.R. as to the total loan of Taka 3,08,35,000/- under the Packing Credit became Taka 2,08,35,000/-. Thereafter, the petitioners; on behalf of their company Janata Fibres International Limited, entered into another contract of sale for supply of jute in bales to Frindown Trading Co. Limited, London. With a view to fulfill the contract, the petitioners' company approached the bank to enhance its Cash Credit Limit. But the bank instead approved for opening back to back L/C for Taka 1,97,70,000/- on certain terms and conditions to enable the petitioners' company to boost up export and generate profit for reduction of the excess over limit and Packing Credit outstanding of Taka 2,08,35,000/-, as this was the trading loss suffered by the petitioners' company in the earlier contract which is the subject matter of the first allegations in the F.I.R. Accordingly, barge receipts of Bangladesh River Service were submitted with the bank for obtaining Packing Credit facility as desired by the bank. Besides to amount of Taka 66,00,000/- (Taka sixty six lacs) being the sale proceeds, jute of the balance of amount of Taka 1,20,00,000/- (Taka one crore twenty lacs) only has been taken by the bank in the godowns as pledged after the F.I.R. was lodged. As a result, the aforesaid jute of the balance amount could not be sold out by the petitioners' company to reduce its liability with the bank. Because of the sudden lodging of F.I.R. of the case, the business of the petitioners' company was stopped and the petitioners' company could not continue to adjust its liability with the back. It is mentioned in the petition that both in the case the first and second foreign contract, no cash loan was received from the bank by the petitioners company against the Packing credit m to meet local purchase of jute for export. In both these cases local sellers of jute from whom the petitioners' company purchased jute for export directly paid by the bank through L/C on receipt of jute into the company's godown under the supervision of the bank officials. The allegations challenging the existence of the aforesaid two Inland Carriers namely, Amazon Shipping Line and Bangladesh River Service, are incorrect, false & malafide on the face of it. The said two Inland Carriers are very much in existence and have been carrying on business obtaining trade licence from the Municipal Corporation, Dhaka. The owner of Bangladesh River Service has sworn an affidavit stating that his concern carried jute of the petitioners' company at the relevant time. Similarly, the owner of Amazon Shipping Line has issued a certificate to the above effect which are annexed with application as Annexures 'I' and 'J'. 

 9. Mr. Moinul Hussain, the learned Counsel appearing for the accused-petitioners, has taken us through the First Information Report, charge-sheet and the application for quashing and other papers annexed to the application and submits that the petitioners as Directors of the company do not deny that the loan was taken from the bank concerned by the then Managing Director of the company, Hemayetuddin (now dead) in due course of banking business and the statement of accounts of the bank and the correspondences made with the company by the bank from time to time clearly reflects that it was a loan under the Packing Credit scheme and the said loan having been obtained by the then Managing Director, Hemayetuddin in due course of business deal and not by adopting any fraudulent means or misrepresentation of facts by the said Managing Director or by the present petitioners as Directors and there being no initial intention to cheat or to mis-appropriate and the loan having been admitted the question of mis-appreciation does not arise. The present criminal case is highly motivated and unwarranted and totally unfounded, misconceived and hence the proceeding is liable to be quashed to secure the ends of justice. The learned Counsel then submits that the loan having been sanctioned in the name of the company, liability, if any, incurred thereunder, is a civil liability of the company with the bank and not a criminal liability of the petitioners and as such to allow the present criminal proceeding started in connection with the dues of the bank on account of the loan to continue will be sheer abuse of the process of the court and hence it is labile to be quashed to secure the ends of justice. The learned Counsel also submits that the bank has initiated the criminal proceeding against the petitioners with a view to use the same as a vehicle of oppression and harassment to the petitioners. The underlying purpose of the criminal case is to put undue pressure on the petitioners and thereby enforce repayment of the loan as per dictation of the bank authority. It is also submitted that the petitioners as Directors of the company do not deny the liability of the company but they only dispute the extent of the claim and the civil court is the proper forum to decide the matter and settle extent of such dispute. The learned Counsel submits that the bank authority being conscious of the nature of the claim has already filed a suit for the realisation of the dues with a further prayer for a decree for liquidation of the loan by way of selling properties of the company and of its directors kept in mortgage with the bank and in that view of the matter, the continuation of criminal proceeding will not only cause harassment to the petitioners but also will be an abuse of the process of the court and to secure ends of justice the criminal proceeding is liable to be quashed. 

 11. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and perused the First Information Report, charge-sheet, application for quashment and other papers annexed with the same. The moot question before us is whether the F.I.R. and charge-sheet contain the allegations and statements which, on the face of it, constitute a criminal offence under the Code against the petitioners and if the answer is in the negative, then whether the exercise of the powers of this court under its extra-ordinary jurisdiction as provided under Section 561A Cr. P.C. will be called for to quash the proceeding before allowing the prosecution to lead evidence to prove its case. Along with the above point another question which arises for our consideration is whether institution and pendency of the civil suit claiming the dues on account of loan taken by the company will itself be a bar for the criminal proceeding. For the determination of the above points we are to see the nature of the claim of the Bank and the liabilities incurred by the company on account of the loan arising out of the transactions, behaviour and modus operandi of the parties, before, at the time of and after the loan was secured. The case of Abdul Quader Choudhury and others Appellants in Criminal Appeal No.28 of 1974. Sk. Sarwarudin  Appellant in Criminal Appeal No.29 of 1974 Versus The Sta respondent, reported in 28 DLR(AD)38, has been cited by the learned Advocates of both the sides as an aid to support their respective contentions. It is admitted and consistently held in the above decisions and many other decisions of the Superior Courts that the High Court has the general jurisdiction over all the Criminal Courts subordinate to it and the said power having been codified in the schedule, the High Court Division has inherent power under the Code of Criminal. Procedure to give elect to any order of any such court subordinate to it and can quash a criminal proceeding to prevent the abuse of the process of any such court, or otherwise, to secure the ends of justice. The pertinent question having arisen and posed as to when and under what circumstances the said jurisdiction can and should be exercised by the High Court Division, Ahsanuddin Chowdhury, J., speaking for the court in the case of Abdul Quader Choudhury and others Vs. The State reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38 held:- 

 "If the criminal proceedings in a particular case is in respect of an offence alleged to have been committed by an accused person and it manifestly appears that there is a legal bar against the institution or continuance of the said proceedings, the High Court would the justified in quashing the proceedings on that ground. Cases may also arise where the allegations in the First Information Report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not constitute the offence alleged, in such cases no question of appreciating evidence arises, it is a matter merely of looking at the complaint or the First Information Report to decide whether the offence alleged is disclosed or not. In such cases it would he legitimate for the High Court to hold that it would he manifestly unjust to allow process of the criminal court to be issued against the accused person." 

 In the said case it is also held:— 

 "Some categories of cases may also be indicated where the inherent jurisdiction can and should be exercised for quashing the proceeding. There may he cases where it may be possible for the High Court to take the view that the institution or continuance of criminal proceedings against an accused person may amount to the abuse of the process of the Court or that the quashing of the impugned proceedings would secure the ends of justice." 

 Relying on the above noted passages of the case reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38; Mr. Moinul Hussain, the learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that the instant case falls within the category of cases where interference of this Court by exercising its inherent power has become not only necessary but also imperative to prevent the abuse of the process of the court. 

 Mr. Barua has also cited the case of Faruk Ahmed Vs. Abdul Kader Chowdhury and others reported in 38 DLR.(AD) 18 wherein it is held:— 

 Referring the case of Zakir Hossain & others Vs The State reported in XLII DLR(AD)102, Mr. Barua submits that pendency of the civil suit over the same subject matter cannot itself be a ground for quashing a criminal proceeding but can only give rise to an occasion for staying criminal proceedings till the disposal of the civil suit. 

 14. The consensus of judicial opinion is that it is not possible, desirable or expedient to lay down any inflexible rule which should govern the exercise of this inherent jurisdiction. The exercise of this jurisdiction will depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case. Interference even at an initial stage may be justified where the facts are so preposterous that even on the admitted facts no case can stand against the accused and that a further prolongation of the prosecution would amount to harassment to an innocent party and abuse of the process of the court. There may also arise cases where the allegations in the First Information Report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not constitute the offence alleged, in such cases no question of appreciating evidence alleged arises it is a matter merely of looking at the complaint or the First Information Report to decide whether the offence is disclosed or not. In such case it would be legitimate for the High Court to hold that it would be manifestly unjust to allow process of the criminal court to be issued against the accused person and to allow the same to continue will amount to causing harassment to the accused persons against whom summon has been wrongly issued. Mr. Rowan has cited the case of R.C.P. Guignard petitioner Vs. The State & another reported in P.L.D. 1963 Karachi 868 wherein it is held:- 

 "Criminal   case entirely based on contractual liability civil court best forum for setting dispute unless circumstances disclose criminal liability. Enforcing civil liability by circumvented criminal prosecution will tantamount to the abuse of the process of the Court." 

 In that case the claim of the prosecuting party was based on agreement which was found to be a contractual liability arising out of the agreement executed between the parties. It was also held that the Civil Court is the best forum for settling such matter unless there are circumstances for criminal prosecution is was also held:- 

 "The High court generally does not interfere with the case pending in the subordinate courts and has always desired the cases to be tried there and concluded but if this rule were to be universally accepted lot of mischief is likely to emanate therefrom. The general tendency on the part of the people here is to enforce civil liability by way of resort to a criminal prosecution which is not permissible under law, it is in these cases where the intention of the party is apparent on the face of the record that the party desires to enforce a civil liability by circumvented criminal prosecution then the High Court will always interfere. If the High Court does not prevent such misconceived and frivolous litigation it shall be abdicating its function of giving prompt redress to the party aggrieved. The legislature in its wisdom being conscious of situations of this type had-made a provision of it in Section 561 A Cr. P.C. In my opinion, where a person is enforcing a liability which is entirely civil in nature by resorting to a criminal prosecution, he is doing something which is not warranted by law and if on his complaint any action has been taken and process has been issued it is obviously an abuse of process of Court." 

 For the proposition of law propounded in the case of Raghunath Puri and other Vs. Emperor reported in AIR 1932 Patna 72, A.J. Heywood and another Vs. Emperor reported in AIR 1942 Lahore 134, J.S. Diver Vs. lqbal Qadir and another reported in PLD 1962 Peshwar 167 were relied on. The learned Judge while quashing the proceeding before him observed as follows:- 

 "After giving the arguments addressed at the Bar my earnest consideration, I am clearly of the view that on the facts stated in the complaint, no criminal offence is made out at all and the sole purpose of launching a criminal complaint against the petitioner and his employees was to coerce, harass and humiliate the petitioner and his employee to make payment of the balance of the deposits without having recourse to civil litigation which unfortunately is both cumbersome and expensive. The tendency to use the criminal courts for enforcing a Civil claim is highly improper; and in the present case, I am constrained to say, almost amounts to blackmail." 

 The law relating to quashment of criminal proceeding being an important and interesting subject occupied its place for discussion in many cases before the superior courts of the sub-continent from time to time and above referred to cases are few of them. We would remain content with citing the case of M.M. S.T. Chidambaram Chettir Vs. Shanmugham Pillai reported in AIR 1938 Madras 29 wherein Newsum, J. observed:— 

 15. The instant criminal case has been initiated by the bank against the petitioners who are the Directors of the company, Janata Fibre International Limited, by way of lodging First Information Report against them and Hemayet uddin (now deceased) who was the then Managing Director of the company along with others. From the First Information Report it appears that it relates to a loan sanctioned by the bank to the petitioners' company under the Packing Credit scheme while this company also had business transaction having various accounts maintained with the bank. It is stated in the F.I.R. that Hemayet uddin (now deceased), Managing Director of the company managed to get the said loan and the said Managing Director has since died. First Information Report does not speak of any overt act being done by the petitioners who are the Directors of the company. Nothing has been stated in the F.I.R. as to what part was played by the petitioners as mere Directors for securing the loan. There is nothing to show from the F.I.R and charge-sheet that these accused petitioners by fraudulent means secured the loan from the bank and thus the elements of deception, fraudulent and dishonest inducement for the delivery of the money by the bank to the company being absent, the charge under Section 420 prima facie does not lie. With regard to the charge under Section 405, there is no allegation of entrustment of any money and misappropriation thereof or turning the same for the use of anybody. That being the position, Mr. Barua, the learned Advocate for the State has found it difficult to refute the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and hence could not assert that the allegation constitutes offence under Section 409 of the Penal Code. While conceding that there appears to be no ingredient of Sections 405 and 420 on the face of the F.I.R. and charge-sheet, Mr. Barua argued that there being allegation of production of forged and fake barge receipts before the bank for the purpose of securing loan, existence of prima-facie case under Section 471 of the Penal Code cannot be ignored. The question whether the documents are forged and whether the said documents were produced by the accused petitioners knowing those as forged are to be determined by evidence during trial and cannot be decided now, the learned Advocate for the State re-iterates. In reply to the submissions made by Mr. Barua, Mr. Husein, the learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that the barge receipts procured in the name of the bank as consignor and produced in the court themselves indicate the carriage of jute goods from Daulatpur to Mongla and Chalna by the Amazon Shipping Line and Bangladesh River Service and on this point no evidence is called for as the carriers themselves have filed the affidavit and the declaration that they have been carrying on business in Bangladesh after obtaining licence from the appropriate authority. Furthermore, it has not been stated in the F.I.R. as to how and in what manner the accused petitioners have done the act of forgery or whether they themselves produced papers before the bank knowing those as forged. On plain reading, we also find that the allegations made in the F.I.R. and the charge-sheet do not constitute any prima-facie offence with which they have been charged. From the legal notice, which is found to have been issued by the bank to the Company on 5.2.187 (Annexure 'O'), for the liquidation of the outstanding liability of the company and averments made in the petition regarding the reply given by the company of the petitioners have not been controverted. On our query, the learned Advocate for the State also could not say from the F.I.R., the charge-sheet and the record that any amount was paid in cash to the company and the accused petitioners received the money and misappropriated the same. Let us now consider another aspect of the case to which our attention has been drawn. The learned Advocate submits that the liabilities standing in the name of company has not ever been denied by the accused-petitioners and the Directors or the heirs of Hemayetuddin, the then Managing Director of the company and a civil suit being Title Suit No.34 of 1989 has been instituted in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj, for the realisation of money on account of the loan money under the Packing Credit scheme and the said suit is now pending for disposal. From the plaint of the suit and the legal notice Annexure 'O' referred to above, it appears that the bank authority has not made any allegation of making any fraudulent representation against the company or its Directors for the purpose of securing loan or doing any act of misappropriation of money or that they have produced any document before the court knowing those to be forged. Therefore, we find that the institution of criminal proceeding earlier to the filing of the civil suit was nothing more than a pressure tactics adopted by the bank to secure repayment of loan money as an alternative remedy to civil sort which is admittedly time consuming and expensive. In the instant case, during the pendency of the criminal proceeding, the bank has filed the civil suit on due and proper consideration that appropriate remedy lies in the civil court. Though it cannot be said as a matter of rule of law that criminal proceeding cannot run simultaneously with the civil suit but there may be exception to this general rule and each case will depend upon its facts and circumstances. In this particular case, from the facts revealed in the F.I.R., charge-sheet and the nature of claim made in the plaint of the suit and the notice issued by the bank claiming the money as dues from the accused petitioners company, we find that the criminal proceeding has been resorted to as a substitute to the civil suit. In view of the nature of the claim made in the suit which is pending before the civil court, we are of the opinion that the remedy which was sought for in the criminal proceeding started earlier has now been made in the civil suit. The claim on the face of it being a civil liability, the civil court is the proper forum for allowing the relief sought for. We are of the view that civil court is competent to deal with the matter in controversy and give effective remedy to the aggrieved party. 

 16. For the foregoing reasons, we hold that the continuance of the criminal proceeding will cause unnecessary harassment to the accused-petitioners and for securing the ends of justice the proceeding against the accused-petitioners is liable to be quashed. Accordingly, the criminal proceeding being G.R. Case No.26 of 1986 arising out of Narayanganj P.S. Case No.7(5)86 dated 5.5.1986 under Section 420/406/409 and 114 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, now pending before the Upazila Magistrate (Sadar). Narayanganj, in so far it relates to the accused-petitioners, is hereby quashed.
